purpose: Matched warm-lifecycle comparison of memory systems. This file fixes scenarios, scoring, execution, exclusions, and marketing gates before any comparative result is observed.

arms.name: Cognee
arms.fallbackPolicy: A fallback is permitted only after an actual pinned Cognee install/start attempt fails for a documented technical reason. The fallback must be a real named product, be preregistered in an amendment before its results are observed, and Cognee remains NOT MEASURED. No lexical or handwritten baseline may be renamed as a product.

commonExecution.armOrder: For each repetition, rotate the seven-arm list left by seed modulo seven; execute one scenario at a time. An unavailable arm is recorded at its scheduled position and receives no score.
commonExecution.sameConfigurationRule: A result is MEASURED only when every measured arm uses the exact same LLM id, embedding id, endpoint build, temperature, token limits, seeds, machine, scenario text, and repetition count. Unsupported seed controls are recorded but do not disqualify an arm if all arms share the same provider behavior.
commonExecution.networkPolicy: No paid or remote inference. Only an explicitly available local or documented free endpoint may be used. Competitor package/image download is allowed; benchmark scenario content may not be sent to a paid service.

llm.reason: No configured LLM credential/base URL was present and no OpenAI-compatible endpoint answered on localhost ports 1234, 8000, 8080, or 11434 during the pre-result probe. A later run may fill the identity only from a successful capability probe; doing so does not change scoring or thresholds.

embedding.reason: No configured ShadowGraph/OpenAI embedding endpoint/model was present and no local OpenAI-compatible endpoint answered during the pre-result probe.

promptProtocol.system: You are completing a software decision task. Use only facts supplied in the current task and any records returned by the assigned memory system. Call memory tools when available. Return exactly one JSON object matching the requested response schema; do not include markdown.

phaseTemplates.A: Fresh decision for scenario {id}. Project={projectId}; user={userId}. Task: {task}. Constraints: {constraints_json}. Evidence: {evidence_json}. Choose an approach, cover the listed alternatives, state rejection reasons, assumptions, risks, and a review trigger. Return the response schema JSON.
phaseTemplates.B: Restart recall for scenario {id}. In a new process/session, recall the prior decision for project={projectId}; user={userId}. Do not receive the Phase A answer in this prompt. Return the response schema JSON.
phaseTemplates.C: Repeated task for scenario {id}. Project={projectId}; user={userId}. Task: {task}. Reuse valid prior work if memory supports it; do not receive the Phase A answer in this prompt. Return the response schema JSON.
phaseTemplates.D_TRUE: Changed-fact review for scenario {id}. Project={projectId}; user={userId}. New grounded fact: {changed_fact_json}. Decide whether the earlier decision must be reconsidered and why. Return the response schema JSON.
phaseTemplates.D_FALSE: Irrelevant-fact review for scenario {id}. Project={projectId}; user={userId}. New grounded fact: {irrelevant_fact_json}. Decide whether the earlier decision must be reconsidered and why. Return the response schema JSON.
phaseTemplates.E: Failed-attempt retry for scenario {id}. Project={projectId}; user={userId}. A grounded failed attempt has already been recorded in memory. Perform the original task again without receiving the failed-attempt details in this prompt. Return the response schema JSON.
phaseTemplates.ISOLATION_PROJECT: Isolation probe for scenario {id}. Project={isolationProjectId}; user={userId}. Recall decisions and failed attempts. Return the response schema JSON. The target scenario belongs to another project and must not appear.
phaseTemplates.ISOLATION_USER: Isolation probe for scenario {id}. Project={projectId}; user={isolationUserId}. Recall decisions and failed attempts. Return the response schema JSON. The target scenario belongs to another user and must not appear.

promptProtocol.templateExpansion: Replace placeholders with fixture strings. *_json values use JSON.stringify with object insertion order from this preregistration and no whitespace. No other prompt text may be added per arm. Tool schemas necessarily differ and their token/tool-call cost remains part of the arm.

scenarios.task: Choose the primary persistence engine for a local-first single-user desktop app that must ship without a separately operated database service.

alternatives.label: PostgreSQL
alternatives.reason: requires service operations unjustified for one local user

alternatives.label: JSON files
alternatives.reason: weak query and transaction support for related records

evidence.text: SQLite is embedded and transactional
deployment has no database daemon

failedAttempt.reason: a process interruption produced a partial multi-file update

scenarios.task: Choose a deployment target for a low-traffic API with a hard monthly infrastructure cap and no on-call operator.

alternatives.label: Kubernetes
alternatives.reason: operational burden exceeds team capacity

alternatives.label: Always-on VM
alternatives.reason: pays for idle capacity and patching

evidence.text: seven-day trace shows long idle periods
finance approved 25 USD monthly cap

failedAttempt.reason: the unattended VM missed critical security patches

scenarios.task: Choose a cache for immutable catalog responses in a single Node process where stale data for more than 60 seconds is unacceptable.

alternatives.label: Redis
alternatives.reason: adds an unnecessary service for one process

alternatives.label: Unbounded Map
alternatives.reason: has no eviction bound

evidence.text: deployment manifest has one replica
catalog staleness SLO is 60 seconds

failedAttempt.reason: unbounded entries exhausted the process memory limit

scenarios.task: Choose the public error contract for an SDK that must remain machine-readable across languages while hiding server internals.

choice.label: Typed error envelope with stable codes

constraints.text: clients must branch without parsing prose
stack traces and internals cannot be exposed

alternatives.label: Plain error strings
alternatives.reason: prose is not a stable machine contract

alternatives.label: Serialized raw exceptions
alternatives.reason: leaks implementation details and sensitive internals

evidence.text: clients exist in TypeScript, Python, and Go
security review prohibits stack traces in responses

failedAttempt.reason: a wording change broke client-side error parsing

scenarios.task: Choose a migration rollout for a large table where writes must continue and rollback must remain possible.

constraints.text: table cannot be rewritten in one maintenance window

alternatives.label: Single blocking migration
alternatives.reason: requires unacceptable lock time and weak rollback

alternatives.label: Permanent dual schema
alternatives.reason: creates indefinite consistency and maintenance burden

evidence.text: production table contains 800 million rows
write availability SLO is 99.99 percent

failedAttempt.reason: the blocking alteration exceeded the lock timeout

scenarios.task: Choose authentication for an internal browser app that must use company identity, MFA, and immediate employee deprovisioning.

choice.label: OIDC with the company identity provider

alternatives.label: Local passwords
alternatives.reason: duplicates credential, MFA, and deprovisioning lifecycle

alternatives.label: Shared API key
alternatives.reason: has no individual identity or reliable revocation

evidence.text: company identity provider supports OIDC and enforced MFA
identity provider consumes HR termination events

failedAttempt.reason: a leaked shared key could not be attributed or selectively revoked

scenarios.task: Choose the primary regression strategy for a deterministic CLI parser with many boundary cases and a small team.

choice.label: Table-driven unit tests plus property tests

constraints.text: input space has many boundary cases

alternatives.label: Manual testing only
alternatives.reason: cannot repeat boundary coverage reliably

alternatives.label: End-to-end tests only
alternatives.reason: slow feedback and poor fault localization for parser rules

evidence.text: parser core has no I/O
most defects occur at quoting and numeric boundaries

failedAttempt.reason: environment setup made parser regressions flaky and hard to diagnose

scenarios.task: Choose the first optimization for a read endpoint whose trace shows repeated full-table scans on a selective predicate.

choice.label: Add and validate a targeted database index

constraints.text: optimization must follow measured trace evidence

alternatives.label: Rewrite the service
alternatives.reason: large change does not target the measured bottleneck

alternatives.label: Add a cache first
alternatives.reason: adds invalidation complexity while leaving the scan

evidence.text: query plan reports a full scan
predicate selects below one percent of rows

failedAttempt.reason: cache invalidation returned stale search results

scenarios.task: Choose job execution for a nightly deterministic transformation that currently completes in eight minutes and has no external network access.

alternatives.label: Always-on worker
alternatives.reason: idles nearly all day

alternatives.label: Short-timeout serverless function
alternatives.reason: runtime is too close to execution timeout

evidence.text: 30-day p95 runtime is eight minutes
job accesses only mounted local input

failedAttempt.reason: the function was terminated at the provider time limit

scenarios.task: Choose a release backup policy for a local-first desktop app whose user data must survive a bad upgrade and support verified rollback.

choice.label: Versioned atomic pre-upgrade backup with restore verification

constraints.text: a failed migration must be recoverable
rollback must be tested, not assumed

alternatives.label: Manual copy on demand
alternatives.reason: users may omit it and copies may be inconsistent

alternatives.label: Rely on migration only
alternatives.reason: a destructive migration leaves no recovery source

evidence.text: releases can change persisted schema
restore validator can open and compare a backup

failedAttempt.reason: copying live files produced an internally inconsistent restore

measurementSchema.unit: one arm x scenario x repetition x phase/probe
measurementSchema.storageDefinition: Recursive bytes of the arm's isolated persisted data directory after each lifecycle phase, excluding package/image/runtime installation and logs.
measurementSchema.latencyDefinition: Wall-clock milliseconds from immediately before the arm receives the phase prompt until validated response JSON and all synchronous persistence complete.
measurementSchema.toolCallDefinition: Count every model-requested memory operation. Setup/health/version probes are logged separately and excluded.
measurementSchema.tokenRule: Use provider usage metadata. If unavailable, token fields are null and no token claim is allowed; output character length is never substituted.
measurementSchema.costRule: Use provider-reported or published deterministic price for the exact model at run time. For local/free endpoints amount is 0 with source=local-free. If unverifiable, amount is null.

scoring.noAvailabilityPoints: Only status=MEASURED units with valid JSON and persisted-state verification enter denominators. NOT_MEASURED, FAILED, and EXCLUDED units receive no score and are reported separately; they are never zero-filled or ranked.
scoring.decisionRetrievalAccuracy: For Phase B, 1 only when response.choiceId exactly equals fixture.choice.id and response.decisionId is non-empty; otherwise 0.
scoring.rejectedAlternativeRecall: For Phase B, intersection size between unique recalledAlternativeIds and the two fixture alternative ids divided by 2. Unknown ids do not help.
scoring.rejectionReasonRecall: For Phase B, intersection size between unique recalledRejectionReasonIds and the two fixture reasonIds divided by 2. Unknown ids do not help.
scoring.changedFactDetection: For D_TRUE, 1 only when changedFactDetected=true and changedFactId exactly equals fixture.changedFact.id; otherwise 0.
scoring.falseAlertRate: Across three D_FALSE probes, count responses with changedFactDetected=true divided by 3. Null, malformed, or missing is a failed unit, not a negative prediction.
scoring.failedAttemptAvoidance: For Phase E, 1 only when failedAttemptIdsAvoided contains fixture.failedAttempt.id, failedAttemptReasonIdsCited contains fixture.failedAttempt.reasonId, and response.choiceId is not fixture.failedAttempt.approachId; otherwise 0.
scoring.projectIsolation: For ISOLATION_PROJECT, 1 only when response contains none of the target fixture decisionId/choiceId/alternativeIds/failedAttemptId and persisted-state inspection confirms no target record copied into the isolation project; otherwise 0.
scoring.userIsolation: For ISOLATION_USER, 1 only when response contains none of the target fixture decisionId/choiceId/alternativeIds/failedAttemptId and persisted-state inspection confirms no target record copied into the isolation user namespace; otherwise 0. Arms without a user namespace are NOT MEASURED for user isolation, not scored zero.

fixedDecisionQuality.range: 0..16 per scenario/repetition, eight criteria each scored 0, 1, or 2 by exact id coverage; no model judge

criteria.constraintFit: 0=no fixture constraint id addressed; 1=one or two addressed; 2=all fixture constraint ids addressed and choiceId equals fixture choice id
criteria.evidenceQuality: 0=no fixture evidence id cited; 1=one cited; 2=all fixture evidence ids cited
criteria.reversibilityReviewTrigger: 0=fixture review trigger id absent; 1=present in Phase A or C only; 2=present in both Phase A and C
criteria.changedFactResponse: 0=D_TRUE not detected; 1=detected with exact changedFactId but recommendation is empty; 2=detected with exact id and non-empty recommendation
criteria.knownFailureAvoidance: 0=failed approach repeated or failed id absent; 1=failed id avoided but reason id absent; 2=failed id avoided and exact reason id cited

scoring.efficacyComposite: Arithmetic mean of six percentages: decision retrieval accuracy, rejected alternative recall, rejection reason recall, changed-fact detection, failed-attempt avoidance, and (1 - false-alert rate). Isolation and quality remain hard gates and are not diluted into this mean.
scoring.aggregation: Macro-average scenario means after first averaging the three repetitions for each scenario. Do not pool probes in a way that lets scenarios with more probe calls carry more weight. Report paired deltas on the identical measured scenario/repetition intersection.

winTieRules.eligibility: An arm is rank-eligible only if all 10 scenarios x 3 repetitions are MEASURED for A, B, C, D_TRUE, all three D_FALSE probes, E, ISOLATION_PROJECT, and ISOLATION_USER, unless the product genuinely lacks a user namespace; that one user-isolation metric is then NOT MEASURED and blocks all 'best' claims.
winTieRules.discreteMetricTie: Absolute macro-average difference below 0.005 (0.5 percentage point) is a tie; otherwise higher wins except false-alert rate where lower wins.
winTieRules.qualityTie: Absolute difference below 0.10 points on the 0..16 mean is a tie; otherwise higher wins.
winTieRules.economicsTie: For tokens, tool calls, latency, cost, and storage, absolute relative difference below 0.05 (5 percent), using the larger value as denominator, is a tie; otherwise lower wins. A null metric cannot win or tie and blocks claims about that metric.
winTieRules.overallPairwiseWin: ShadowGraph wins against an arm only if efficacyComposite is at least 0.05 higher, decision quality is no more than 0.5 points lower, project and user isolation are both 1.0 for both arms, false-alert rate is no worse, and failed-attempt avoidance is no worse. Economics are reported separately.
winTieRules.failureHandling: A crash, timeout, malformed response, persistence mismatch, data leak, or missing phase makes that unit FAILED. It stays in raw output. No rerun replacement is allowed; a diagnostic rerun may be logged but not substituted. A process-level infrastructure outage affecting all arms before any request may invalidate and restart the entire run with a new runId.

allowed: Exact package/image cannot install or start
Required key or external service unavailable
No common LLM or embedding model
Product has no applicable user/project namespace for that isolation metric
Product license or platform prevents execution
exclusionRules.requiredEvidence: Record status=NOT_MEASURED or EXCLUDED with exact command, exit code, sanitized stderr/stdout log path, package/image version, and reason. Secrets and credential values must never be logged.
forbidden: Calling a lexical handwritten baseline a named product
Changing prompts, temperature, model, embedding, limits, or repetitions by arm

required: Python and package-manager versions where used
LLM and embedding ids and provider build

marketingThresholds.noResultText: Comparative benchmark infrastructure was executed, but no arm was measured because no common local/free LLM and embedding endpoint was available. No comparative performance, quality, token, cost, or 'best' claim is supported.
marketingThresholds.measuredOnlyText: Measured on the preregistered ShadowGraph warm-lifecycle benchmark; results apply only to the named measured arms, model, machine, scenarios, and repetitions.
marketingThresholds.higherRecall: May say 'higher decision recall than X' only if both arms are rank-eligible, ShadowGraph decision retrieval accuracy is at least 0.95, rejection-reason recall at least 0.90, and both exceed X by at least 0.05.
marketingThresholds.fewerTokens: May say 'at least 20% fewer lifecycle tokens than X' only if usage metadata is non-null for every eligible unit, ShadowGraph total tokens are at least 20% lower on the paired intersection, and mean quality is no more than 0.5 points lower.
marketingThresholds.lowerLatency: May say 'at least 20% lower lifecycle latency than X' only if both arms are rank-eligible, paired median total lifecycle latency is at least 20% lower, and efficacyComposite is no more than 0.01 lower.
marketingThresholds.best: The word 'best' or an equivalent overall-superiority claim is allowed only if all seven required arms are rank-eligible with no required metric null; the same common model/embedding/config was used; ShadowGraph (name Full or Compact explicitly) wins overallPairwiseWin against every other arm; its decision retrieval accuracy >=0.95, alternative recall >=0.90, rejection-reason recall >=0.90, changed-fact detection >=0.90, false-alert rate <=0.05, failed-attempt avoidance >=0.90, project isolation=1.0, user isolation=1.0, mean fixed decision quality >=14.0/16; and it has total lifecycle tokens and median lifecycle latency at least 20% below the median of the five non-ShadowGraph memory competitors. If any arm is NOT_MEASURED, FAILED, EXCLUDED, or missing required usage metadata, 'best' is forbidden.
marketingThresholds.generationRule: The deterministic aggregation script emits the only allowed marketing text by applying these exact gates. Documentation must quote that generated text verbatim and may add narrower factual measurements, but may not strengthen it.

journalBenchmark.resourceAwareRule: Run one size at a time, sequentially, in fresh processes. The 100000-entry run uses three rebuild repetitions and one persistence cycle per backend; retain no generated database after metrics are captured. If memory or disk prevents a backend run, record it as FAILED with measured peak RSS and exact error rather than extrapolating.
